- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum or volatility.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual market action.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when recent history includes strong downward moves, failing to capture rebound potential.
- Underreacts to sharp price spikes in the history — forecasts remain flat or slightly downward even after a spike, missing the momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, then undercorrects upward after strong downward moves.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast often show higher error than first 10–15, suggesting model struggles with short-term volatility near end of window.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model should adjust upward by 1–2% per day to avoid underestimating momentum.
